newsitem.title: CANADA: Mark's Work Wearhouse to buy Work World.
newsitem.headline: Mark's Work Wearhouse to buy Work World.

text.p: Canadian clothing retailer Mark's Work Wearhouse Ltd said on Monday it agreed to buy all shares of Work World Enterprises Inc, which operates 157 franchised stores in Canada, for C$6.7 million.
Mark's said Work World, which runs stores under the Work World and Workwear World banners, generates annual sales of C$90 million.
Mark's operates 106 corporate and 34 franchise stores with total sales of C$280 million.

In its first full year of combined operations, the 300-store merged firm was expected to generate sales of C$400 million, making Mark's the largest specialty men's retail clothing chain in Canada, it said.
Mark's presdient Garth Mitchell said Work World stores average 3,000 square feet and are located in smaller markets. Mark's own stores average 10,000 square feet and operate in larger centers.
He said undeveloped Canadian markets provided potential to add at least 75 more stores, most in the smaller format.
Mark's said it intended to operate the newly acquired locations as a separate division.
The purchase, expected to close in the next few weeks, was to be financed with term debt to be placed with the company's bank.
Mark's said the acquisition was expected to provide incremental earnings per share in the short term and growth potential in the long term. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
